title: Functional versatility of synergid cells in plant reproduction
authors: Ling Li, Honghui Lin, Li-Jia Qu, Sheng Zhong
abstract: In this review, Li et al. discuss the diverse functions of synergid cells at different reproductive stages, including pollen tube guidance, pollen tube reception, and fertilization recovery, to ensure double fertilization success in flowering plants. They also highlight unanswered scientific questio…

title: Postnatal Pax7-expressing limb cells are multipotent and generate non-myogenic lineages that persist into adulthood
authors: Stamatia Gioftsidi, Takuto Hayashi, Sidy Fall, Sabrina Jagot, Matthieu Dos Santos, Fabien Le Grand, Frederic Relaix, Philippos Mourikis
abstract: Gioftsidi, Hayashi, et al. uncover that in mouse neonatal hindlimb muscles Pax7 progenitors generate both myogenic and non-myogenic cells, including a specific subpopulation of fibroblast-like cells, which they call Pax7FAPs. This multipotency declines with age, but perinatally-derived Pax7FAPs can…

title: Senescent cells maintain viability through adhesion-dependent fragmentation that promotes debris deposition
authors: Matej Durik, Mona Karout, Daniel Sampaio Gonçalves, Tania Knauer-Meyer, Coralie Spiegelhalter, Nadia Messaddeq, Marco Seehawer, Pauline Stephan, Dmitry V. Bulavin, Yann Herault, Lars Zender, William M. Keyes
abstract: Durik et al. show that senescent cells generate fragments, termed SCAFs, that support survival by shedding damaged intracellular material. SCAF rupture releases DAMPs, amyloid-like proteins, and bioactive cargo, promoting wound-healing and cancer-associated programs. These findings identify fragment…

title: The ARLA1A-NAC089 module coordinates ER phagy with the unfolded protein response to maintain cellular homeostasis in plants
authors: Lianming Yang, Weixin Luo, Tingting Huang, Shuo Wang, Zhiran Cao, Dong Jiang, Lei Pang, Jian-Xiang Liu, Sicong He, Ruixi Li
abstract: Yang et al. reveal that the ARLA1A-NAC089 module couples ER phagy with the UPR in plants. This dual regulatory axis fine-tunes cell survival versus death under stress, providing a mechanistic framework for maintaining ER homeostasis and enhancing environmental resilience.

title: A VHL-HIF signaling axis orchestrates invariant natural killer T cell development and fate decisions
authors: Qian Li, Chao Zhang, Anshu Tang, Jia Li, Yun-Cai Liu
abstract: Li et al. show that the VHL-HIF axis controls invariant NKT cell development. VHL loss stabilizes HIF1α, which drives iNKT cell apoptosis and blocks iNKT2 fate via mitochondrial metabolism, and HIF2α, which suppresses iNKT17 specification through IL2RA-STAT5 signaling, impairing antitumor immunity.

title: A thermoregulatory module for timekeeping in Arabidopsis
authors: Yuqing He, Xiling Wang, Chen Su, Yufan Niu, Yumei Qin, Jiashuo Zhang, Lei Wang
abstract: He et al. show that PRR9 contributes to thermal adaptation by transmitting temperature signals and maintaining a relatively stable circadian period across a range of temperatures. The study provides insight into how the circadian clock mediates diurnal and seasonal temperature-sensing.

title: Systematic differences in protein stability underlie species-specific developmental tempo
authors: Mitsuhiro Matsuda, Henrik M. Hammarén, Jorge Lázaro, Mikhail M. Savitski, Miki Ebisuya
abstract: Using dynamic SILAC proteomics, Matsuda et al. show that protein degradation is globally slower in human than in mouse segmentation clock cells. Glycolysis inhibition in mouse partially phenocopies the human protein stability profile, linking metabolism, protein stability, and developmental tempo.

abstract: Why do mammalian species develop at different speeds? authors: Giacomo Furlan, S. Bryn Martin, Brandon Cho, Ying Yu Ng, Sarah A. McClymont, Abdul Rahman, Elizabeth J. Robertson, Evelyne Collignon, Miguel Ramalho-Santos
abstract: Furlan et al. show that TGF-β signaling, previously thought to be dispensable for pre-implantation mouse development, is essential for blastocyst diapause, a reversible state of embryonic dormancy. Nodal-Smad2 signaling is specifically required for survival of dormant embryos and embryonic stem cell…

authors: Jinwoo Lee, Ahri Kim, Yideul Jeong, Eugene Choi, Tae Young Kim, Mariam Nabukenya, Daesik Kim, Jaecheol Lee, Gyu-Un Bae, Jong-Sun Kang
abstract: Lee and Kim et al. generate elongating heart organoids (EHOs) from human induced pluripotent stem cells. EHOs undergo elongation and looping-like morphogenesis and establish venous-arterial axial patterning with venous pole-initiated contractile propagation. EHOs provide a human platform to study ea…

authors: Du Kong, Peng Lin, Yifan Guo, Kai Lin, Sihua Zhao, Shuai Yang, Xianping Wang, Guangzhao Zhu, Lesi Xie, Shotaro Tatekawa, Jiadong Zheng, Wenyan Xu, Li He, Hideshi Ishii, Bin Jin, Kangwen Cheng, Qi Xie, Xianjue Ma
abstract: Intratumoral heterogeneity fuels cancer progression through poorly understood cooperative mechanisms. title: Senescent cells: Leaving cellular waste behind
abstract: Cellular senescence is one of the best-studied biological programs, yet it continues to reveal unexpected aspects. In this issue of Developmental Cell, Durik et al. describe how senescent cells shed large cytoplasmic fragments that promote their survival and may represent a mechanism of communicatio…

title: Between adaptation and cell death: An ER-localized transcription factor controls cell fate
abstract: Rooted in place, plants must continually balance adaptation and cell death under environmental stress. In this issue of Developmental Cell, Yang et al. demonstrate that NAC089, an ER-localized transcription factor, acts as a molecular switch that determines these alternative outcomes under different…

title: Two HIFs, two fates: VHL-HIF signaling controls iNKT cell identity
authors: Kyung Min Yim, Jin Young Huh, Jae Bum Kim
abstract: Invariant natural killer T (iNKT) cells acquire effector identity during thymic development, yet how metabolic and signaling programs regulate iNKT cell fate remains unclear. In this issue of Developmental Cell, Li et al. elucidate that the VHL-HIF axis with HIF1α and HIF2α modulates survival and di…

title: Slowing down on hot days: How morning PRR9 controls the pace of the plant circadian clock
abstract: The circadian clock maintains a nearly constant pace across a wide range of temperatures in plants. In this issue of Developmental Cell, He et al. reveal how condensation of the morning clock protein PRR9 and its protein-protein interactions mediate high temperature sensing and adjust the pace of th…

title: Skeletal muscle stem cells keep their lineage options open
abstract: Expression of Pax7 has been widely used as a hallmark of muscle stem cell identity, and genetic deletion of Pax7 compromises skeletal muscle regeneration. In this issue of Developmental Cell, Gioftsidi, Hayashi et al. use lineage-tracing approaches to report that other skeletal muscle cell types als…

title: Protein turnover rate sets the developmental clock
abstract: In this issue of Developmental Cell, Matsuda et al. and Nakanoh et al. reveal that global protein turnover rate controls species-specific developmental clocks. Their findings demonstrate how translation and degradation rates regulate embryonic timing, raising the possibility that cells directly sens…

title: Nodal/Smad2 signaling maintains diapause in the mouse embryo
abstract: Embryonic diapause is a reversible dormant state that allows mammalian blastocysts to survive periods of environmental or metabolic stress. In this issue of Developmental Cell, Furlan et al. report that Nodal/Smad2 signaling sustains diapause by repressing Pparg-driven lipid storage in the blastocys…

title: Growth factor receptor corralling fuels persistent leader-bleb dynamics
abstract: Jha et al. show that confined melanoma cells establish migratory polarity by restricting EGFR mobility at the bleb rear, using CD44 and ezrin-radixin-moesin (ERM) proteins as diffusion barriers rather than directional cues.
